title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were not designed to handle the combination of extreme traffic congestion, extended idle periods, and consequent battery depletion that occurred during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco. At least a dozen vehicles became stranded, unable to navigate out of gridlock near the Golden Gate Bridge, and one caught fire after driving over fireworks in the roadway. The deployment failed because the system was used in conditions far outside normal operating parameters, with traffic volumes and duration that exhausted battery reserves.

The failure point was in operational planning rather than the autonomous driving technology itself. Waymo lacked either the foresight to avoid routing vehicles into predicted severe congestion during a major holiday event, or a protocol to preemptively withdraw vehicles from service when such conditions were forecast. A human dispatcher with authority to redirect or stage vehicles before gridlock developed could have prevented the stranding.

It is not established whether the vehicle fire was caused by a defect in the autonomous system or solely by external hazards on the roadway.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations. At least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, ran out of battery power while stuck in severe traffic congestion near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Video evidence showed numerous stationary vehicles lined up on streets, with at least one requiring a flatbed truck for removal. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off in the roadway.

Waymo stated its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and indicated the company is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during major traffic disruptions. Frustrated motorists reported spending hours in standstill traffic, with some expressing anger at the driverless vehicles blocking roadways. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with public and private partners to improve future events. This represents another operational challenge for Waymo in San Francisco, following a December incident when a power outage caused some of its vehicles to stall at intersections with nonworking traffic lights.
